note.note:
H&P – Super Detailed Note  

Consult Summary:  
28-year-old woman with no significant past history presents via tele-consult with a first-ever, left occipital throbbing headache of 24-hour duration, severity 8/10, without red-flag associated features; treated empirically with stronger NSAID + paracetamol, advice on hydration/rest, and safety-net instructions given.

History:  
• Presenting complaint: New-onset headache.  
• Onset/Timeline: Began yesterday mid-morning; gradual build-up to current intensity, persistent since.  
• Location: Left posterior/occipital region of head.  
• Character & Severity: “Intense,” throbbing, rated 8/10.  
• Course/Progression: Stable; not worsening at particular times of day; single episode so far.  
• Exacerbating/Relieving factors: No change with lying, standing, bending, coughing, or sneezing. Single dose of ibuprofen provided little relief.  
• Associated symptoms – negatives specifically denied:  
  – Nausea, vomiting, anorexia.  
  – Visual disturbance, blurred vision, photophobia (“funny lights”), eye pain.  
  – Focal neurological symptoms: tingling, numbness, weakness, speech difficulty.  
  – Constitutional: fever, chills, sweats.  
  – Rash, neck stiffness.  
• Systems review: Normal appetite, hydration, and overnight sleep; no recent illness, sinus/nasal symptoms, trauma, or medication changes mentioned.  
• Prior episodes: None; patient states headaches are unusual for her.

Past Medical History:  
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No previous similar headaches.  
• No asthma or gastrointestinal conditions.

Medications:  
• None regularly.  
• Ibuprofen (Nurofen) – single dose yesterday; dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:  
• None known (patient denied allergies).

Social History:  
• Lives with partner in apartment; private setting for call.  
• Occupation: Designer (desk-based).  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: Denies regular use.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies.  
• No recent lifestyle, dietary, or stress changes identified.

Family History:  
• Mother: Hypertension, migraines.  
• No other familial disorders discussed.

Physical Examination:  
Tele-consult; no objective findings recorded.  
• Vitals: Not obtained.  
• General/Neurologic: No focal deficit, meningeal signs, or visual disturbance reported by patient.

Investigations:  
• None performed or ordered during visit.

Assessment & Plan:  

Issue 1 – New-onset unilateral throbbing headache (probable primary headache, likely migraine vs tension-type):  
  – Assessment: First headache episode; features suggest migraine without aura given unilateral throbbing pain and maternal migraine history, though absence of classic migraine accompaniments keeps tension-type in differential. No red-flag features elicited.  
  – Plan:  
    • Initiate stronger NSAID (specific agent not documented) to be taken regularly with food, in place of ibuprofen.  
    • Add paracetamol concurrently (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
    • Advise rest, adequate oral hydration.  
    • Safety-net: Seek medical review if pain worsens, fails to settle within 1–2 days of treatment, or if red-flag symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, neurological change, recurrent episodes).  
    • Consider in-person evaluation including neurological exam and blood pressure measurement if no improvement.

Issue 2 – Health maintenance / blood pressure screening:  
  – Assessment: Patient unaware of recent BP despite family history of hypertension.  
  – Plan: Arrange routine BP check with primary care provider or pharmacy at earliest convenience.

Issue 3 – Patient education & follow-up:  
  – Assessment: First headache causing functional impairment; patient requested prognosis.  
  – Plan: Explained expected course (should improve over next 1–2 days); provided instructions to contact service if not improving or if concerned.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):  
1. Migraine without aura – Likelihood: High.  
   • Supports: Unilateral throbbing pain, severe (8/10), female in twenties, positive maternal migraine history, no focal deficits.  
2. Tension-type headache – Likelihood: Moderate.  
   • Supports: Lack of nausea/photophobia, persistent ache, possible occupational stress/posture; Opposes: Unilateral location, pulsatile quality, high severity.  
3. Cervicogenic headache – Likelihood: Low-Moderate.  
   • Supports: Occipital location, sedentary desk work; Opposes: No neck pain or positional aggravation.

Quality checks (document_quality):  
● Missing but expected: Objective vitals, full neurological & fundoscopic exam, documented allergies (“none” recorded but could verify), detailed medication doses, menstrual/OCP history.  
● Transcript/DDx conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; complete information for remote visit but lacks physical examination.
